candidate: For dyadic blocks of even N, prove sum |C_Lambda(N) - N*S(N)|^2 = o(X^2), where C_Lambda is the ordered von Mangoldt convolution and S is the conventional Goldbach singular series.
conditional_implication: If D(X) <= c_* X/4 and block_energy < c_*^2 X^2/16, then there is no residual exception N in [X/2,X], where c_*=2*C2 and D(X)=2 floor(log_2 X) floor(sqrt(X)) (log X)^2.
proof_dependencies: A residual target with R(N)=0 has P_Lambda(N)=0 because N/2 is composite
A single dyadic coefficient contributes its squared discrepancy to the block energy
independent_derivation: The block L2 norm bounds each coefficient discrepancy by its square root; this gives a uniform o(X) discrepancy and contradicts the linear singular-series main term at any zero representation.

published_estimates_checked.source: Bhowmik and Grimmelt 2026, Theorem 3.1 and equation (3.8)
published_estimates_checked.status: does not prove candidate; ordinary zero-real-part parameter cannot be below 1/2 because zeta has infinitely many zeros on Re(s)=1/2

first_missing_theorem: An unconditional dyadic mean-square discrepancy estimate o(X^2), or an explicit block bound below c_*^2 X^2/16 after prime-power correction.
countermodels: An abstract one-exception block with W_N=cN has energy c^2*N0^2 >= c^2*X^2/4 for N0 in [X/2,X], so O(X^2) with an unrestricted constant does not suffice.
claims_not_made: No proof that the proposed energy estimate holds
No proof of universal residual coverage
